items.title: DeepChem-DEL: An Open-Source Framework for Reproducible DEL Modeling and Benchmarking
items.abstract: DNA-encoded libraries (DELs) allow screening of extremely large chemical spaces by tagging compounds with DNA barcodes. Machine learning (ML) techniques have enabled the extraction of meaningful chemical patterns from noisy, target-specific DEL binding data. However, existing tools for DEL machine learning (DEL-ML) remain fragmented, which limits systematic construction and reproducibility of modeling pipelines. Moreover, this fragmentation hinders integration of new models, such as chemical foundation models, into DEL workflows alongside classical approaches. To address these challenges in DEL modeling, we introduce DeepChem-DEL, an open-source suite of reproducible ML workflows for DEL modeling built on the DeepChem ecosystem. DeepChem-DEL integrates (i) a configurable denoising pipeline with (ii) modular DeepChem workflows for enrichment prediction, hit identification, and benchmarking across diverse model classes, including chemical foundation models enabled through extensions to the open-source ChemBERTa-3 framework. We evaluate DeepChem-DEL on the KinDEL and BELKA data sets, reproducing key baselines and enabling direct comparison across model classes. Our experiments demonstrate that leveraging chemical foundation models yields performance competitive with, and in several cases exceeding, previously explored approaches such as graph convolutional networks and random forest models. Together, these results demonstrate that DeepChem-DEL is a scalable and extensible platform for DEL-ML, while highlighting the potential of chemical foundation models for improved DEL modeling and prioritization.

items.title: Deepfake Image Detection Using Transfer Learning Techniques
items.abstract: The rapid advancement of deep learning and generative artificial intelligence has enabled the creation of highly realistic artificial images and videos, commonly known as deepfakes. These manipulated media pose significant challenges to digital security, identity verification, privacy, and information authenticity. Consequently, developing reliable techniques for detecting deepfake content has become an important research challenge. This study proposes a deep learning-based approach for detecting manipulated facial images using transfer learning with the MobileNetV2 architecture. The experimental dataset consists of 1,081 real facial images and 960 fake facial images, with the latter obtained through frame extraction from videos available in the FaceForensics++ dataset. The pre-trained MobileNetV2 model is adapted for binary classification by incorporating global average pooling, a fully connected dense layer, dropout regularization, and a sigmoid output layer. The model is trained to classify facial images into two categories: real and fake. Its performance is evaluated using standard classification metrics, including accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, confusion matrix, Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curve, and Precision-Recall curve. The experimental findings demonstrate the potential of transfer learning for identifying manipulated facial images using a lightweight convolutional neural network architecture. The study highlights the applicability of MobileNetV2 for deepfake image classification under limited-data conditions and identifies dataset diversity and generalization across different sources as important considerations for further research.

items.title: DeepSkin: A Segmentation-Guided Deep Learning Framework with Generative Augmentation for Dermoscopic Skin Cancer Classification
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence has considerable potential to support dermoscopic skin cancer assessment; however, class imbalance, heterogeneous lesion morphology, indistinct lesion boundaries, and imaging variability can limit model generalizability. This study presents DeepSkin, a segmentation-guided deep learning framework integrating lesion segmentation, generative augmentation, and lesion-focused classification. Dermoscopic images were first segmented using a bidirectional ConvLSTM-based U-Net (BCDU-Net), and the resulting lesion regions were used for region-of-interest (ROI) extraction. During classifier development, a conditional generative adversarial network (cGAN) generated class-conditioned synthetic lesion ROIs to increase training-data diversity and mitigate class imbalance. Real and synthetic training ROIs were subsequently used to train a fine-tuned VGG16 network for binary benign–malignant classification. The framework was developed using the ISIC 2016 dataset, comprising 900 training and 379 test images, and independently evaluated on the PH2 dataset. On ISIC 2016, DeepSkin achieved a Dice coefficient of 0.937 and an intersection over union (IoU) of 0.882 for lesion segmentation, together with a classification accuracy of 96.6% and a receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC-AUC) of 0.981. Cross-dataset external evaluation on the independent PH2 dataset, conducted without retraining or fine-tuning, yielded a classification accuracy of 95%. Ablation analysis further demonstrated incremental performance improvements associated with preprocessing, segmentation-guided ROI extraction, and generative augmentation. Grad-CAM visualizations provided qualitative insight into image regions contributing to classification decisions. These findings suggest that integrating generative augmentation with segmentation-guided lesion classification can support accurate dermoscopic image analysis across independent datasets. Further evaluation using larger, diverse, multi-center and prospective clinical datasets is required to establish broader generalizability and clinical applicability.

items.title: Deliberation Within AI: A Reproducible Pipeline for Multi-Agent Deliberation Simulation
items.abstract: Recent advances in generative AI have renewed interest in whether large language models can simulate aspects of public deliberation. Current deliberation simulations remain methodologically fragile: fluent conversational outputs are often treated as evidence of deliberative quality despite limited reproducibility, weak safeguards for viewpoint diversity, and limited systematic evaluation. This article argues that AI-deliberation simulations can function as credible analytical instruments only if they incorporate infrastructures for reproducibility, plurality preservation, and deliberative quality assessment. The article develops a stage-structured method for deliberative simulation combining persona validation, plurality auditing, and discourse-quality assessment within a reproducible pipeline. The framework is presented as a methodological proof-of-concept and evaluated through a simulation study on the June 2023 Swiss federal referendum on the Climate and Innovation Act together with a batch replication study comparing direct and structured deliberation architectures. The findings show that, as an integrated theory-driven architecture, the structured pipeline generates more stable deliberative dynamics than unconstrained interaction, including clearer plurality preservation and more coherent opinion updating. At the same time, the simulations remain below human minipublics in terms of contextual grounding and justificatory depth. The article positions AI-deliberation simulations as methodological infrastructures for cumulative and empirically testable research on AI-supported deliberation in digital governance.

Variabel penelitian yaitu penilaian audit internal SMK3 yang dikumpulkan melalui observasi, wawancara, dan telaah dokumen menggunakan lembar checklist berdasarkan Peraturan Pemerintah No.50 tahun 2012. Introduction: PT X Surya Panel has high potential risk of workplace hazards, making the implementation of an Occupational Health and Safety Management System (OHSMS) essential to prevent occupational accidents and protect workers from hazard. An internal OHSMS audit is required to evaluate the extent of OHSMS implementation at PT X Surya Panel Semarang. Method: this study employed a quantitative descriptive evaluative approach conducted in 2024. The sample consisted of 20 employees was selected using purposive sampling. The research variable was the internal OHSMS audit assessment. Data collected through observation, interviews, and document review using a checklist based on 64 criteria stipulated in Government Regulation of the Republic of Indonesia No. 50 of 2012 concerning the Implementation of Occupational Health and Safety Management Systems. Results: The overall internal OHSMS audit achievement score was 76.56%, which categorized as good. However, 7 major nonconformities and 8 minor nonconformities identified. Improvements needed, particularly in the establishment of the Occupational Health and Safety Committee, incident reporting and monitoring systems, to improve the effectiveness and sustainability of OHSMS implementation. Conclusion: The overall implementation of the OSHMS at PT X Surya Panel Semarang categorized as good based on the internal audit assessment, with an achievement score of 76.56%. Nevertheless, priority improvements are required in OHSMS policies, the establishment and functioning of P2K3, incident reporting, and management review.

items.title: Detection of AI-Generated and Deceptive Fake Reviews on E-Commerce Platforms Using Lightweight Machine Learning
items.abstract: Product reviews shape what people buy, yet their credibility is under a fresh threat: large language models (LLMs) can now mass-produce reviews that are fluent, varied and grammatically flawless. Current detectors cope with this only in part. The best-performing published systems lean on transformer models, paid LLM interfaces or reviewer metadata, resources that smaller platforms often lack, whereas lighter classical models were largely designed around older, human-written spam. We compare five recent studies of fake-review detection, looking at their data, labelling, methods, reported accuracy and acknowledged limitations. Two patterns emerge: accuracy tends to rise together with computational cost, and some of the highest accuracies rest on heuristic or weakly supervised labels, which casts doubt on what they actually measure. Drawing on these observations, we propose a lightweight, interpretable pipeline that pairs TF-IDF n gram features with stylometric indicators of machine generated text and compares four classifiers: Naïve Bayes, Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machine and Random Forest. The accompanying evaluation protocol is fully specified and includes stratified hold-out and cross validation, cross-generator and cross-domain tests, paraphrase robustness and ablation. Experimental results for the proposed pipeline are not included in this version, and no performance figures are claimed for it. The system is intended as a risk-scoring aid for human moderators, never as proof of AI authorship.

items.title: Developing and validating the Chinese version of the Perceived Trustworthiness of Large Language Models Scale (PT-LLM-8)
items.abstract: The trustworthiness of technology constitutes a critical determinant of user adoption, particularly regarding artificial intelligence (AI) in daily life. Currently, prominent AI products rely on large language models (LLMs), and such LLMs assist users in personal and professional contexts. To systematically investigate the perceived trustworthiness of LLMs, we provide a psychometrically sound measurement instrument for assessing perceived trustworthiness of LLMs. Given the importance of the Chinese market for current AI developments, the present study examined the psychometric properties of a Chinese version of the Perceived Trustworthiness of Large Language Models Scale (PT-LLM-8) [1] and its association with Big Five personality traits, self-efficacy, and self-esteem. Based on the responses of 478 Chinese adults, the Chinese PT-LLM-8 showed good psychometric properties, including strong internal consistency and a clear unidimensional factor structure. Evidence of construct validity was provided by theoretically expected associations between PT-LLM-8 score and self-efficacy, self-esteem, Agreeableness, and Conscientiousness. These findings provide psychometric support for the Chinese version of the PT-LLM-8 as a measure of perceived trustworthiness of LLMs, consistent with the cumulative cross-linguistic evidence for the instrument across its English [1], German [2] and Chinese versions.

items.title: Development and educational evaluation of iLN, a DeepSeek-based generative AI platform for teaching lupus nephritis: a randomized controlled, single-blind (outcome assessor-blinded) study
items.abstract: Lupus nephritis (LN) is the most common and severe organ manifestation of systemic lupus erythematosus, and its diagnosis and treatment require the integration of clinical, serological, and renal pathological information. Few studies have evaluated generative artificial intelligence (GAI)-assisted teaching dedicated to LN training. We developed an interactive LN teaching platform (iLN) based on the DeepSeek large language model, integrating current textbooks, guidelines, a renal pathology atlas, and authentic cases across seven modules. In a randomized controlled study, 50 third-year medical students were randomized in a 1:1 ratio to iLN-based multimodal teaching (iLN group) or traditional lectures (control group). Randomization was performed using a random number table after all participants had been enrolled, and the outcome assessor was blinded to group allocation. The primary outcome was an immediate postintervention 20-item multiple-choice examination (100 points). The iLN group achieved a higher median score compared to the control group (median 90 [IQR 90–95] vs. 75 [IQR 75–80]; Hodges–Lehmann median difference of 15.0 points, 95% CI 10.0–20.0; Mann–Whitney U test P < 0.001). There was no significant difference in score dispersion between the groups, as the 95% confidence interval for the ratio of standard deviations included 1.0. The nominally smaller standard deviation does not provide evidence that the platform reduced variation in learning outcomes. Additionally, iLN students reported a high satisfaction rate of 96.0%. The iLN platform was associated with higher immediate post-intervention test scores and high student satisfaction, supporting the feasibility of integrating generative AI into a multicomponent platform for LN. Larger multicenter studies with validated instruments and long-term follow-up are required. NCT07706998 (retrospectively registered on June 30, 2026).

items.title: Development of a Virtual Reality Learning Environment for Computer Assembly Competency in Pre-Service Teachers Using Generative AI-Produced Media
items.abstract: Thai computer teacher trainees must assemble and repair computers during their practicum, yet many get little hands-on practice because laboratory machines are scarce, outdated, and easily damaged. This design-and-development study built a virtual reality learning environment (VRLE) for computer assembly on a Meta Quest 3 headset, with controller-free hand tracking, three simulation rooms mapped to a national occupational competency unit, and learning media produced with generative AI. Development followed the ADDIE model, and a feasibility tryout used a one-group pretest–posttest design. Three content experts and three technical experts rated content (M = 4.74) and technical quality (M = 4.45) as very good, with interaction and usability the weakest domain (M = 4.11). Among 35 pre-service teachers with matched tests, achievement rose from 8.20 to 9.09 out of 10 (Wilcoxon z = 2.95, p = .002, r = .50; t(34) = 2.92, dz = 0.49). After a sequence of website lessons, VR practice, real-hardware practice, and debriefing, mean competency on real hardware was 4.85 (n = 36) and mean satisfaction was 4.79 (n = 28), both with ceiling effects. Without a control group, the results show that the VRLE is feasible and well received, not that it caused the gains.

items.title: Development of research competence of undergraduates through training in text linguistics based on artificial intelligence
items.abstract: Introduction This study addresses the development of undergraduates' research competence through teaching Text Linguistics by integrating artificial intelligence tools. The study aims to develop a scientific and methodological model and experimentally evaluate its effectiveness. Methods A mixed-methods quasi-experimental design was employed involving 58 first-year undergraduates enrolled in the Kazakh Language and Literature educational program. The experimental group consisted of 30 students, while the control group included 28 students. ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity AI, Elicit, Consensus, and Scite.ai were integrated into tasks involving scientific text analysis, academic writing, literature review, evaluation of scientific evidence, and research reflection. Research competence was assessed using a 100-point test, scientific text analysis tasks, a Likert-scale questionnaire, and an expert assessment rubric. Statistical analyses included descriptive statistics, the Shapiro-Wilk test, paired and independent t-tests, Cohen's d, and Cronbach's alpha. Results The experimental group's research competence score increased from 58.43 ± 6.87 to 84.27 ± 5.94 points. The improvement was statistically significant ( p < 0.001), with a large effect size (Cohen's d = 1.92). Discussion The findings indicate that the systematic pedagogical integration of artificial intelligence tools into Text Linguistics instruction can support the development of undergraduates' scientific text analysis, academic writing, critical thinking, evidence-based reasoning, and research independence.

items.abstract: Introduction This study examined changes in students' self-reported creativity-related behaviors following an educational intervention combining artificial intelligence (AI) tools and the DRAE instructional model (Diagnosis, Recreation, Application, and Estimation). Methods A one-group preexperimental pretest-posttest questionnaire design was complemented by semi-structured interviews and direct-observation records. The quantitative analysis included 551 valid paired EvaCreIA records, exceeding the minimum sample target of 543. The questionnaire assessed Generate Diverse Ideas (GID), Generate Creative Ideas (GIC), and Evaluate and Improve Ideas (EMI). Complementary interview indicators were calculated from 703 eligible pretest and 730 eligible posttest records, while direct observation included 568 completed checklist records. Results Posttest means exceeded pretest means by 0.222, 0.270, and 0.241 points for GID, GIC, and EMI, respectively, on a five-point scale. Wilcoxon signed-rank comparisons remained statistically significant after Holm adjustment ( p < .001). Rank-biserial correlations were 0.340 for GID, 0.387 for GIC, 0.340 for EMI, and 0.374 for the supplementary overall score. The complementary interview indicators showed higher favorable-response percentages at posttest. Discussion The results indicate changes in self-reported creativity-related behaviors following the combined educational intervention. However, retrospective record linkage, limitations in cross-instrument correspondence, self-report measurement, and the absence of a comparison group restrict causal interpretation. The findings do not establish an independent causal effect of AI or validate the DRAE model.

items.title: Digital Agriculture and Plant Genomics for Predictive Breeding
items.abstract: Digital sensing, genomic prediction and increasingly accessible computational methods are changing how crop breeders observe environments, characterise genetic variation and prioritise candidate varieties. Yet the central question is not whether more data improve predictive fit, but whether combining information sources produces reliable, timely and economically worthwhile selection decisions outside the circumstances in which models were trained. This critical narrative review examines the convergence of plant genomics, field phenomics, environmental characterisation and artificial intelligence in predictive breeding. Peer-reviewed research and methodological literature published from 2001 to 11 September 2026 were critically selected through accessible scholarly sources and citation tracing, with attention to empirical comparisons, validation design and translational relevance. Genomic prediction provides a well-established foundation, whereas phenomic and environmental covariates yield more conditional benefits. Contrasting wheat studies illustrate that spectral and thermal information can improve prediction in some settings but can also introduce noise or fail under forward validation. Environmental descriptors become more informative when aligned with developmental stage and the target population of environments; flexible machine-learning architectures do not consistently outperform appropriately specified statistical baselines. Structural variation, pangenomes, multi-omics and genomic language models broaden the biological information available to breeders, although evidence of additional realised genetic gain remains limited for several emerging approaches. Major weaknesses include information leakage, unrepresentative validation partitions, incompatible field metadata, uncertainty neglected during selection, and scarce evaluation of operational costs and varietal delivery. The review develops a decision-centred framework in which data collection, model complexity and evaluation are governed by the breeding decision and the information genuinely available at that point. The strongest near-term opportunities lie in prospective multi-environment validation, careful phenomic measurement, stage-aware environmental modelling and interoperable datasets. Predictive breeding is therefore best understood as a disciplined integration of biological understanding, field experimentation and statistical evidence, not as a replacement for them.

items.title: Digital technologies in construction material manufacturing: A systematic review of applications, performance outcomes, and integration frameworks
items.abstract: The construction sector consumes roughly 36 percent of global energy and generates 40 percent of carbon dioxide emissions, which makes the way building materials are produced a pressing sustainability problem. This paper reviews, systematically, how digital technologies are applied in construction material manufacturing. The review pursues three aims: to identify the main technology domains, to assess what they deliver in practice, and to propose a conceptual framework for their integration. Searches of Scopus and Web of Science returned 112 peer-reviewed studies, which were analysed thematically and mapped bibliometrically. Five principal domains emerged: artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) for quality prediction; Internet of Things (IoT) process monitoring; additive manufacturing (AM); digital twin (DT) simulation; and Building Information Modeling (BIM) combined with lifecycle assessment (LCA). The evidence points in one direction. Product quality, operational efficiency and environmental performance all improve, with material waste falling by 30–60 percent, prediction errors by 18–17 percent, and procurement lead times by 27 percent on average. Combination matters more than any single tool: gains grew substantially when technologies were used together rather than alone, so integrated adoption outperforms a piecemeal one. The proposed framework offers practical direction for manufacturers, researchers and policymakers working on the digital transformation of construction material production.

items.title: DIGITALIZATION, CIRCULARITY AND GEOPOLITICAL RISKS AS DRIVERS OF GLOBAL FASHION INDUSTRY DEVELOPMENT
items.abstract: The article investigates the transformation of the global fashion industry in the first half of the 2020s under the combined influence of digitalization, circularity and geopolitical risks. Its purpose is to explain how these drivers reshape value creation, the geography of production, market access and the economic security of global value-chain participants. The study applies systemic and structural-functional approaches, comparative analysis, content analysis of regulatory requirements in major importing markets and elements of scenario-based synthesis. A development driver is defined as a persistent factor that, over several business cycles, changes costs and value added, the spatial organization of production and sales, and the institutional conditions of international trade. An integrated analytical framework is proposed that connects the three drivers with four transmission mechanisms: costs, speed, regulatory compliance and demand. Digitalization influences product development, forecasting, supply-chain coordination and traceability; however, artificial intelligence may either limit excess production or accelerate the proliferation of short-lived collections. Circularity creates additional value through resale, repair, rental and material recovery, while requiring reliable product information and reverse logistics. Geopolitical risks, including trade restrictions, logistics disruptions and origin verification, shift sourcing priorities from the lowest purchase price towards supply reliability and compliance. The analysis identifies complementarities between digital identification and circular operations, supply-chain visibility and resilience, and local reuse and reduced dependence on distant manufacturing. Conflicts arise when accelerated assortment renewal undermines circular objectives, nearshoring raises production costs, or new compliance requirements disadvantage smaller suppliers. The resulting configuration of global value chains combines geographically diversified sourcing, verifiable product data, reverse flows and supplier selection based on resilience rather than price alone. Four operational criteria are suggested: the number of genuinely alternative production nodes, the share of products with a verifiable digital record, the ability to reallocate production within a quarter and the availability of circular arrangements in priority markets. For Ukraine, opportunities for nearshore supply to the European Union depend on the capacity to manage wartime disruptions, demonstrate traceability and upgrade beyond cut-make-trim operations towards product development and digital order support. The scientific contribution consists in interpreting the interaction of three drivers through a common economic framework and translating this framework into practical criteria for export and supply-chain strategies.

items.title: Disaster Robotics in the Deep Learning Era]{Disaster Robotics in the Deep Learning Era: A Systematic Review of Platforms, Autonomy, Methods, Datasets, Challenges, and Future Research Directions
items.abstract: Disaster robotics enables responders to sense and act at a disaster site from a safe distance, converting responder risk into an equipment one. The field is increasingly shaped by deep learning and, most recently, by foundation models. However, existing surveys adopt a single perspective or platform class, predate the deep learning era or remain largely narrative. Moreover, none grades every reviewed work on a common validation maturity scale. This paper presents a systematic review of disaster robotics in the deep learning era, restricted to disaster-connected works evaluated on disaster data or in real, replicated or simulated emergency settings. The evolution of the field is traced through successive research phases, from teleoperated platforms to foundation-model interfaces and responder-grounded field autonomy. A multi-criteria taxonomy is formed, covering response tasks, robotic platforms, perception, autonomy, learning strategies, foundation model types, human-robot teaming, coordination, communication and deployment, disaster domains, and validation maturity. Each criterion is analyzed comparatively, with critical insights into the strengths and limitations of its categories under field conditions. Additionally, public datasets and benchmarks are reviewed. Current challenges are also paired with future research directions, from data acquisition and field hardening to verifiable autonomy, responder trust and evaluation. The analysis shows that systems deployed at real incidents still rely predominantly on model-based methods. It also shows that recent research leans increasingly on simulation and benchmark evaluation. Finally, foundation models have entered the field mainly as perception front ends and mission-level planners rather than as embodied policies, without yet reaching a real incident.

items.title: Divergent Uptake of Apology as Admission or Commitment: Why One Apology Can Be Heard as Several Different Promises
items.abstract: This conceptual paper introduces Divergent Uptake of Apology as Admission or Commitment, a mechanism by which a single apology is understood by different recipients as containing different admissions or commitments. An acknowledgment may be taken as conceding a particular wrong, promising future action, or asking for forgiveness. The expectations formed through these readings can extend beyond what the speaker stated, while the public meaning of the act cannot be reduced to the speaker's private intention. The paper assesses an apology by distinguishing the scope of admission, undertaking, forgiveness, and repair. It asks what the speaker acknowledged, on whose behalf, what was promised or excluded, and what different recipients took the act to settle. A sincere apology may leave an unresolved issue untouched, and an accepted admission does not establish forgiveness or completed repair. Divergent interpretations require evidence of what recipients understood, rather than an assumption that disagreement or dissatisfaction reflects misunderstanding. The discussion places the mechanism alongside J. L. Austin's account of uptake in speech acts and examines two documented cases. After the Netherlands defeated Mexico in the 2014 World Cup, Arjen Robben apologized for diving earlier in the match while maintaining that the winning penalty was legitimate. Published reports assigned his admission to different incidents, with shortening and translation complicating the record. In December 2020, CD Projekt Red apologized for the console release of Cyberpunk 2077 and directed dissatisfied customers toward refund procedures. One reader understood the letter as implying an exception to Sony's normal policy, while another understood that the store retained authority over refunds. The company subsequently confirmed that no special refund arrangement existed at the time of the apology. Part of the Trust, Participation, and Repair series within On Human Modeling, the paper examines who defines what an apology admitted, who may declare repair or forgiveness complete, and what evidence supports competing interpretations. Potential applications in human–AI research include conversational repair, institutional apologies, customer-support systems, and evaluations that distinguish acknowledgment from commitment, forgiveness, and completed remedy.

items.title: Does Learning from Unlabeled Data Help Cancer Diagnosis and Prognosis? Semi-Supervised and Self-Supervised Learning Versus Tabular Foundation Model
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Machine learning for cancer diagnosis and prognosis requires costly patient labels. Semi- and self-supervised methods exploit unlabeled data but are rarely tested against equivalent supervised models. We tested whether unlabeled data help and compared these methods with a tabular foundation model. Methods: Four public breast cancer datasets (WDBC, Mammography, METABRIC, SEER) crossed clinical task (diagnosis, including the detection of microcalcifications on Mammography, or prognosis) with class balance. In five-fold cross-validation with five seeds, 10%, 20%, or 50% of training records were labeled. Self-training (random forest and XGBoost), label spreading, and SCARF self-supervised pretraining were each compared with a matched supervised control; logistic regression and TabPFN v2 were references. Analyses used corrected resampled t-tests with Holm adjustment, Bayesian correlated and hierarchical tests, and power analysis. Results: Of 96 comparisons with matched controls in the Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) and the area under the precision–recall curve (PR-AUC), three were significant, all involving SCARF: two losses on Mammography and one PR-AUC gain on METABRIC that persisted with all labels. The estimated minimum detectable effects at 80% power varied across comparisons, with medians of approximately 0.06 in PR-AUC and 0.09 in MCC; the median absolute observed differences were 0.008 and 0.015, respectively. At the default threshold and 10% labels, label spreading lowered sensitivity on SEER (−0.135) and random-forest self-training on Mammography (−0.122). TabPFN had the highest PR-AUC in all 16 settings. Conclusions: Under the evaluated datasets, methods and settings, no statistically significant additional benefit from unlabeled data beyond shared preprocessing was detected, but the evidence does not establish equivalence; TabPFN achieved the highest PR-AUC in every setting. New methods should be tested against matched controls and tabular foundation models with adequate power.

items.title: Early Detection of Ovarian Cancer: Current Strategies and Future Directions
items.abstract: Ovarian cancer (OC) is a major cause of cancer-related mortality among women worldwide, mainly because most cases are diagnosed at advanced stages due to non-specific early symptoms. Although early detection is essential for improving clinical outcomes, accurate and accessible screening remains a major challenge, owing to the non-specific nature of early symptoms, the pronounced histological and molecular heterogeneity of the disease, and the poor performance of conventional screening approaches based on cancer antigen 125 (CA-125), human epididymis protein 4 (HE4) and imaging modalities. This review outlines the major biological and technical challenges in the early diagnosis of OC, briefly summarizes the value and limitations of conventional diagnostic approaches and focuses on current progress in emerging biomarkers, including circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA)/cell-free DNA (cfDNA) alterations, exosomal biomarkers and mesothelin multi-marker combined detection strategies, and novel technologies, such as artificial intelligence, nanotechnology, single-cell sequencing and biosensors for early detection. We also discuss the advantages, current limitations, practical considerations and translational barriers of these approaches. Future advances in OC screening will require the integration of sensitive biomarkers, multimodal detection strategies and more accessible, cost-effective technologies to improve early diagnosis and patient survival.

items.title: Edge Intelligence in Precision Agriculture: A Multimodal IoT-Driven Framework for Predictive Eustress Management in Medicinal Plants, with Statistically Validated Reinforcement-Learning Control
items.abstract: Medicinal plants grown under water stress are not simply surviving it—many respond to a mild, well-timed drought by producing more of the secondary metabolites that make them valuable, provided the stress never tips into outright damage. Growers call the useful kind eustress and the harmful kind distress, and keeping a crop inside that narrow window is a harder control problem than ordinary irrigation scheduling, especially once a cloud-connected system has to add network latency and tolerate dropped links into the mix. This paper proposes an edge artificial intelligence (AI) and Internet of Things (IoT) framework that pairs a MobileNetV2–LSTM–Transformer fusion design with a Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) irrigation agent, keeping the whole decision loop local to the field. The fusion network itself is not trained here; what we test is the control policy alone, in a reproducible simulation of the eustress decision problem. No accuracy metric for the fusion network, no energy measurement and no secondary-metabolite outcome is reported; the stress band and distress threshold are generic modeling choices, and every control result is a property of the simulator. Five independently trained PPO agents were compared against four baselines—no irrigation, a constant dose, a threshold rule, and a carefully tuned PID controller—on 30 shared held-out weather scenarios using paired statistical tests with Holm–Bonferroni correction. The learned policy did not beat the threshold and constant-dose rules on band occupancy (13.7% versus 14.3–15.6%), and the tuned PID controller clearly outperformed it there (32.8%, p < 10−4). PPO reached the lowest distress exposure, only reaching distress 7.4% of the time, compared with 12.4–74.2% for the baselines (p < 10−4), but this is a trade-off of the tested configuration (λ3 = 6), obtained at higher water use (406 L versus 0–259 L) and lower band occupancy than the tuned PID; it is not a general advantage over PID. Pushed into an unseen heatwave, both PPO and PID held onto partial control (61.0% and 72.8% distress) while the remaining baselines essentially collapsed (about 99% distress). A reward-component ablation and a weight sweep trace this behavior back to the distress penalty specifically, with a smaller penalty weight trading some of that distress protection for higher band occupancy. No single controller came out ahead on every measure we tracked.

items.title: Education Management Strategies in Facing the Challenges of the Digital Era
items.abstract: Purpose – This study examines education management strategies for addressing interrelated challenges of digital transformation and develops an integrated interpretation of institutional management priorities in the digital era. Design/methods/approach – A descriptive-qualitative literature review examined relevant national and international scholarly publications, emphasizing research from 2021–2026 alongside selected foundational studies. The sources were organized by recurring institutional challenges and interpreted through thematic comparison and narrative synthesis. Findings – Four interconnected challenges were identified: unequal digital infrastructure and access, limited digital competence, resistance to organizational change, and ethical and data-security risks. Corresponding priorities include inclusive infrastructure planning, continuous professional development, participatory digital leadership, and accountable governance of educational data and artificial intelligence. Addressing these priorities together offers a more coherent managerial response than isolated technology initiatives. Research implications/limitations – The synthesis offers practical considerations for institutional planning and a conceptual basis for future empirical evaluation. As a narrative review, it cannot establish causal effects, determine the relative prevalence of barriers, or compare intervention effectiveness across educational settings. Originality/value – The article connects established digital transformation challenges with complementary management responses, emphasizing the coordination of technological, human, organizational, and ethical dimensions rather than technology adoption alone.

items.title: Educational service quality in higher education: A systematic review and thematic synthesis of qualitative and mixed-methods evidence
items.abstract: This review synthesized qualitative evidence on how students, staff, leaders and employers conceptualize and perceive educational service quality in higher education. Following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020 statement, a Scopus search of articles published between 2020 and 2026 identified 890 records. After artificial intelligence-assisted title and abstract screening, validated manually on a random sample, and full-text assessment by two authors, 27 qualitative and mixed-methods studies were included. Quality was appraised with the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool, and findings were analyzed through thematic synthesis. Seven analytical themes and 22 sub-themes were identified: teaching and academic quality; physical, digital and learning infrastructure; administrative and student support services; employability, practice and personal development; relational and co-created quality; institutional and organizational conditions; and well-being, safety and basic needs. All themes were retained in sensitivity analyses, although support for employability depended largely on weaker studies. Read through a structure–process–outcome lens, the themes distinguish the institutional and basic conditions of the service, its academic, administrative and relational processes, and its expected outcomes. Compared with established instruments, institutional conditions were absent, whereas basic needs, co-creation and labor-market links were insufficiently specified. The findings are limited by a single English-language database search, six unretrieved reports and the interpretive nature of the framework. Quality assurance may benefit from approaches that also consider the conditions under which educational services are produced.

items.title: Effectiveness of an Artificial Intelligence-Based Facial Gesture-Controlled Game in Dysphagia Rehabilitation Following Traumatic Brain Injury
items.abstract: Objectives: To compare AI-based gamified therapy with conventional orofacial physiotherapy in improving swallowing function, therapy compliance, and oral intake among individuals with post-traumatic brain injury dysphagia. Material and Methods: In this pilot randomized controlled trial, 10 participants aged 18–60 years with post-traumatic dysphagia, minimum Rancho Los Amigos Level 5, and Glasgow Coma Scale ≥12 were randomly assigned to AI intervention or conventional therapy groups. Interventions were delivered 5 days/week for 4 weeks. Outcomes included the Dysphagia Outcome and Severity Scale (DOSS), Functional Oral Intake Scale (FOIS), Self-Reported Compliance Scale, and Ryle?s tube-to-oral transition. Non-parametric statistical tests were used. Results: The AI group demonstrated significant improvements in DOSS ( p = 0.004, r = 0.80) and FOIS ( p = 0.039, r = 0.84). Between-group differences were significant for DOSS ( p = 0.011, r = 0.80) and FOIS ( p = 0.017, r = 0.84). Compliance was significantly higher in the AI group ( p = 0.012). Among the three intervention-group participants who were Ryle’s tube dependent at baseline, two (66.7%) transitioned to full oral intake, compared with none of the two tube-dependent participants in the conventional therapy group ( p = 0.30). Conclusion: AI-powered gamified therapy shows promising preliminary benefits in swallowing recovery, therapy compliance, and functional oral intake following traumatic brain injury. Larger randomized controlled trials are warranted.

items.title: Effects of instructional format on knowledge outcomes in risk assessment training: A four-arm quasi-experimental study
items.abstract: Background Risk assessment training is a core component of occupational health and safety (OHS) education, requiring conceptual integration and procedural reasoning. With the increasing use of digital technologies, instructional content is delivered through various formats; however, comparative evidence for conceptually demanding OHS topics remains limited. Objective To compare the effects of four instructional formats—slides, podcast-only, slide + podcast, and video—on knowledge outcomes and participant evaluations. Methods A four-arm quasi-experimental pre-test–post-test design was conducted among health-related vocational school students (pre-test n = 188; post-test n = 183). Participants were assigned based on academic programs; individual-level matching was not possible due to anonymous data collection. Group comparisons were performed using non-parametric tests (Kruskal–Wallis, Mann–Whitney U with Holm correction), and effect sizes were reported. Results Pre-test scores differed slightly (p = .027, ε 2 = .034). Post-test scores showed significant differences with a moderate effect (p < .001, ε 2 = .203). The slide + podcast group achieved the highest scores (g = 1.74), followed by the slide group (g = 1.04). Minimal changes were observed in the podcast-only (g = 0.14) and video groups (g = 0.11). These g values reflect independent-sample differences rather than within-person change. Training evaluation scores differed (p < .001, ε 2 = .113), with higher ratings in multimodal formats but no difference between them. Conclusions Instructional format is associated with learning outcomes in risk assessment training. Multimodal approaches may better support learning in conceptually complex OHS content; however, findings should be interpreted as a pedagogical pattern rather than causal superiority.

items.title: El secreto represivo y los ecos de la dictadura: los archivos de inteligencia en Uruguay y sus procesos de institucionalización y reconstrucción digital
items.abstract: This article examines the preservation, institutionalization, and opening up of documentary heritage relating to human rights violations committed during and in connection with Uruguay's last period of dictatorship (1968–2004). Taking the discovery of the Berrutti Archive in 2006 as its starting point, the article examines the transition from repressive secrecy to the establishment of a normative and institutional framework shaped by international standards and the demands of transitional justice. It also assesses interdisciplinary initiatives undertaken at the Universidad de la República, with particular emphasis on the data cross-referencing methodology developed by Proyecto Cruzar and the citizen science platform LUISA. Finally, the article addresses the developments and ethical and methodological dilemmas arising from the application of artificial intelligence, multimodal models, and knowledge graphs to degraded collections of repressive documentation. It concludes that the integration of archival rigor, technological innovation, and community participation is indispensable for consolidating the right to truth, collective memory, and guarantees of non-repetition.

items.title: EMERGING TECHNOLOGIES AND SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT IN NIGERIA: CHALLENGES FOR DIGITAL LEARNING SYSTEMS
items.abstract: The emergence of digital technologies, without doubt has continued to reshape educational systems across the globe, creating new opportunities for sustainable development in developing countries such as Nigeria. This study examines the nexus between emerging technologies and sustainable development with particular emphasis on digital learning systems in Nigeria. The increasing adoption of artificial intelligence, cloud computing, virtual learning platforms, mobile technologies, and digital communication tools has significantly transformed teaching, learning and knowledge dissemination in educational institutions. Despite these advancements, challenges such as inadequate technological infrastructure, poor internet connectivity, digital inequality, limited technical skills and inconsistent policy implementation has continued to undermine the effectiveness of digital learning systems in Nigeria. The paper adopts qualitative approach and makes use of secondary sources of data to bridge the gap in knowledge. The study examines the role of emerging technologies in promoting sustainable digital learning systems in Nigeria, identify the challenges associated with the adoption of digital learning technologies in educational institutions; and investigate the challenges affecting the effective integration of emerging technologies into Nigeria's educational system. The paper hinges on the Technology Acceptance Model and Diffusion of Innovation Theory as its theoretical frameworks. While Technology Acceptance Model explains users' acceptance and utilization of digital technologies based on perceived usefulness and ease of use. The diffusion of Innovation Theory provides insight into how technological innovations spread are adopted within educational and social systems. The paper concludes that although emerging technologies possess significant potential for transforming Nigeria's educational landscape and advancing sustainable development, deliberate investments in infrastructure, digital literacy, and supportive policies are necessary for achieving long-term effectiveness and inclusiveness

items.title: Ethical considerations in AI-enabled electrocardiography: a narrative review
items.abstract: Introduction Artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled electrocardiography (ECG) can detect arrhythmias, structural abnormalities, and physiological patterns not readily apparent through conventional interpretation. However, its rapid clinical integration raises ethical concerns. This review critically synthesizes literature on bias and fairness, privacy and confidentiality, explainability and transparency, clinical trust and automation bias, and governance and accountability. Methods We conducted a narrative review using structured searches of PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science. Review preparation was informed by the SANRA quality-assessment scale, and study selection was summarized using a flow diagram adapted from PRISMA-ScR (435 records identified; 46 studies included). Studies were eligible if they substantively examined ethical considerations in AI-ECG; those addressing technical performance alone were excluded. Evidence was classified by study design and clinical maturity. Results Ethical risks arose throughout the AI-ECG lifecycle, beyond the algorithm itself. Studies documented performance disparities across sex, age, race, and ethnicity, alongside vulnerabilities involving membership inference, biometric re-identification, and unintended attribute inference. Explainability remained inadequately evaluated, while automation bias raised concerns about clinical decision-making and patient safety. Governance and post-deployment oversight remained fragmented. Most quantitative evidence came from retrospective or experimental proof-of-concept studies rather than externally validated or clinically deployed systems. Discussion Responsible AI-ECG implementation requires a lifecycle approach addressing upstream bias, privacy safeguards, clinically meaningful explanations, clinician oversight, and post-deployment surveillance. We propose Inherent Protocol Bias (IPB) as an organizing framework linking downstream ethical risks to decisions in study design, data collection, validation, and deployment. Unlike dataset bias, selection bias, spectrum bias, measurement bias, and cohort-origin confounding, which describe specific sources or manifestations of error, IPB emphasizes the protocol-level decisions through which established biases arise or persist. IPB is not a new statistical form of bias but a framework for identifying actionable intervention points. We outline potential applications for improving fairness, privacy, accountability, and clinical trust; however, these recommendations remain conceptual and require empirical evaluation.

items.title: Ethical Dilemmas of AI Use in PAI Learning: A Teacher's Perception and Grade X Students' Learning Behaviors at MA As Syakur
items.abstract: The use of artificial intelligence (AI) in Islamic Religious Education (IRE) offers opportunities to enhance students’ understanding but also raises ethical concerns regarding academic honesty and the accuracy of religious information. This study aims to analyze AI use, teacher perceptions, students’ learning behaviors, and the ethical dilemmas arising at MA As Syakur. Employing a descriptive qualitative approach, the study involved one IRE teacher and eight Grade X students selected purposively. Data were collected through interviews, classroom observations, and documentation of 33 student assignment books, then analyzed thematically. The findings reveal five patterns of AI use, ranging from seeking explanations and comparing information to directly copying AI-generated answers. items.title: Ethical Dimensions of Computational Social Science Research: A Primer
items.abstract: This primer discusses the ethical questions raised by computational social science (CSS), that is, research that analyses data generated at scale by digital platforms, networked devices, and public administrations. Much of the ethical guidance available to CSS researchers was developed for clinical and interventional research, and it assumes a bounded study, an identifiable participant, and an occasion on which consent can be sought. Since much CSS research lacks these features, the primer examines where this guidance fits and where it does not. The primer is organised around six themes: data, privacy, and power; bias and equity; conceptual clarity and value-laden choices; stakeholder impact, justice, and participatory research; ethical communication and public engagement; and the use of generative AI in the research process. Each theme is introduced conceptually, illustrated with cases from the published literature, and followed by reflection questions that researchers can ask of their own projects. The primer is intended for researchers, research ethics committees, and teaching. It pays particular attention to research on administrative registers, including data held by Statistics Netherlands. The research for this publication was partly funded by ODISSEI, the Dutch national research infrastructure for the social sciences.
